recentItems.title: US strike hits Iran wedding party | DW News
recentItems.description:
The US launched its first airstrikes on Iran in more than a month, saying it targeted IRGC forces preparing to deploy sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials say a US missile struck a house hosting a wedding in southern Iran’s Hormozgan province, killing several people, including a child, and wounding dozens. CENTCOM described its strikes as limited and precise against minelaying forces and did not directly address the civilian casualty reports. Iran said it retaliated with ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Jordan; the IRGC claimed US casualties, while US officials said there were none.

#iran #usa #missilestrike #dwnews

recentItems.title: Why destroyed books are about more than paper in Ukraine | DW News
recentItems.description:
What if one of the biggest targets in a war wasn't a military base, but a printing press?
After a Russian drone strike hit Ranok, one of Ukraine's largest children's publishers, thousands of books were destroyed.
The strike raises a question that goes beyond military strategy: what happens when a war also hits culture, education and the stories meant for the next generation?

recentItems.title: Why millions in Africa still lack power | DW News
recentItems.description:

On a continent where energy from the sun, wind and other sources could be in abundance, 600 million still lack reliable access to power. recentItems.title: Pentagon upheaval after Driscoll resignation | DW News
recentItems.description:
The resignation of US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has added to uncertainty inside the Pentagon. Seen as a champion of military modernization and reportedly at odds with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Driscoll leaves a vacuum at the top of the Army, which now lacks both a Senate-confirmed civilian secretary and military chief. Michael O'Hanlon of the Brookings Institution joins us to assess the implications.
